_comment: One row per FlagGems CI run, written by report-feishu.
Field names are identical to the keys of record.json from
collect_gems_record.py, so reporting is a direct key-by-key mapping with
no translation table. Adding a field means editing BOTH files: a field
only here shows up as an empty column, and a key only there is silently
dropped, since report_feishu.py skips keys the table does not have.
Types: 1=text 2=number 5=datetime(ms since epoch) 7=checkbox 15=url.
The records API reads Number fields back as strings; the field type is
still Number, so sorting and aggregation work in the table UI.
record_id        dedup key, '<run_id>-<run_attempt>-<backend>'. Includes
run_attempt, so an auto-rerun is a new row rather than
overwriting the failed attempt.
kind             'test' (PR) or 'baseline' (push)
backend/runner   e.g. 'tsingmicro' / 'tsingmicro3.6'
flaggems_tag     FlagGems release tested, also the asset directory name
flagtree_sha     commit under test: PR head for test, github.sha for
baseline
flagtree_branch  base_ref for test, ref_name for baseline
pr_number        empty for baseline runs
pr_url/run_url   links back to GitHub
actor            GitHub login that triggered the run
job_status       ordered by how early the pipeline broke, so an upstream
failure is never masked by a missing later stage:
build_failed, test_failed, no_baseline, regression,
success. 'no_baseline' means no comparison ran at all
(the first baseline on a runner), which is not the same
as having compared and found no regression.
best_updated     baseline runs only: whether this run became the new
best baseline
collected_at     when the record was assembled
-- this run, absolute: straight from summary.json ---------------------
tested_at           when the test run itself started
duration_s          wall clock across all test jobs
marks_collection_ok false means operator markers were not collected and
the counts below are unreliable
total_ops           operators attempted
total_cases         test cases attempted
passed/failed/skipped/errors
not_found           operators with no test case at all
pass_rate_all       passed / total_cases, matching the comparison report
pass_rate_run       passed / (passed + failed + errors), excluding
skipped. THE ONLY RATE COMPARABLE ACROSS BACKENDS:
each backend skips a different operator set, so a
denominator containing never-run cases is not
meaningful between backends.
skip_operators_cnt  size of the skip list this run used
skip_operators      the list itself, comma separated. Lets a jump in
pass rate be attributed to a compiler change rather
than to an operator having been added to a skip list.
-- delta vs baseline: from compare_report.json ------------------------
All of these stay empty when no comparison ran; the keys are always
present so every row has the same shape.
compared         whether a comparison happened at all
baseline_ref     which baseline the deltas are against, read from the
baseline dir's commit_id.txt, '<date> : <commit>'.
Without it the deltas have no reference point.
verdict          ACCEPT or REJECT, plain token, 1:1 with the comparison
script's exit code. Only regressions block a merge;
warnings are visible in warnings_cnt instead.
regressions_cnt  test cases that got worse (passed -> failed/error/...)
improvements_cnt test cases that got better
warnings_cnt     changes worth attention but not blocking, e.g.
failed -> error
info_changes_cnt changes with no verdict impact, e.g. failed -> skipped
new_operators_cnt / removed_operators_cnt
operators present in only one of the two runs
delta_*          candidate minus baseline for cases/passed/failed/
skipped/errors
regressed_ops / improved_ops
operator names, comma separated
Operator-level rows are deliberately NOT a table here: ~420 operators x
10 backends per run is thousands of rows a day. They stay in the local
Ledger/operators/<record_id>.jsonl instead, and carry per-operator
status, change_type and failed_cases for trend analysis.
